landed_against.rule: R-17 — the slice declares its pair diffs here and the capture is its own commit

why: No golden scenario armed a rune, so the two keystones that own the auto-attack schedule itself — Hail of Blades and Lethal Tempo, the only names damage._auto_attack_timestamps reads a swing list from — had zero golden coverage and lived on unit tests alone. Both rewrite state.num_auto_attacks before the rotation is priced, so a regression in either moves every auto, on-hit, crit and stacking-penetration number in the fight and nothing in the committed set would have seen it.

The section is a pair-jurisdiction addition only: it enters through pipeline.run_fight like every other fight in this snapshot, so the coupled baseline is untouched and its difference set stays empty.

qualifying_population.rule: Adding a snapshot section can move exactly two things: the section itself, which is one absent_to_value membership transition, and the four derived shape counters metadata.fingerprint publishes over the sections. It cannot move a leaf of an existing section, because no scenario already in the snapshot passes a keystone — golden_snapshot._run_fight built every FightParams with the default empty rune page before this slice and still does for every other caller.
qualifying_population.method: 'golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json --report' at the slice tip, before the capture.

/metadata/fingerprint/sections.cause: the new section's name, sorted into the published list

/metadata/fingerprint/entries.cause: two top-level entries, one per KEYSTONE_FIGHT_CHAMPIONS holder

/metadata/fingerprint/leaves.cause: the 24 fight summaries the section adds and their breakdown rows

/metadata/fingerprint/numeric_leaves.cause: every leaf the section adds is a rounded number; it carries no strings

scenario_shape.why_two_range_classes: both runes state their bonus attack speed as a melee/ranged pair, and Lethal Tempo its bolt damage too, so one range class would leave half of every declared number unexercised
scenario_shape.why_the_empty_arm: the control: the same champion, build, level and length with an empty page, so a moved leaf is attributable to the rune rather than to the auto stream underneath it
scenario_shape.why_those_lengths: Hail's window is its initial stacks inside a 3s stack duration, so 5s prices it whole; Lethal Tempo stacks to its cached maximum of six over a 6s stack duration and fires its bolt only at that cap, so 12s is the shortest length here that reaches it, and at 12s Hail's window is long expired — which is what makes the fight prove the schedule reverts rather than staying fast
scenario_shape.why_deterministic: the build is crit-capable and damage.py rolls per swing, so the capture would not reproduce without it (CLAUDE.md, Known Quirks)
